newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy does not want delay in EMU launch - Dini.
newsitem.headline: Italy does not want delay in EMU launch - Dini.

text.p: Italy's Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini was quoted on Monday as saying Italy wanted European economic and monetary union (EMU) to proceed on time even though he thought an extra year of preparation would be helpful.

Italian news agency ANSA quoted Dini, attending a meeting of European Union foreign ministers in Luxembourg, as saying that Italy "wants to go ahead (with EMU) according to the programme and the calendar which have been established."

The Socialist-led left-wing election victory in France and the row between the Bundesbank and the German government over a plan to revalue gold reserves suggested he may have been right in saying previously that another year to prepare for EMU would be useful, Dini said.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi has staked his political career on taking Italy into the first wave of EMU, planned for launch in 1999.

"I do not hide that already some months ago I said that another year would have been helpful for everybody. At the time, my opinion was interpreted as request for a delay. It is nothing of the sort," Dini was quoted as saying.
"The events in Germany and France show that maybe I was right," he added.
